content.thinking:
I'm working out how to phrase the symptom for the postmortem — trying to pin down whether it's specifically account pages or shop pages generally that slowed down, based on the p95 latency metric and the affected service.

For the cause, I'm tracing it to account page renders doing quadratic work per request due to the lifetime average spend calculation running on every render with the flags disabled — I need to verify this mechanism against the actual code that ran to confirm the loop structure matches the claim.

The next step is pinning down the specific deploy that introduced this: revision 5e07d73 rewrote average_spend_per_item to re-sum the purchase list on each loop iteration instead of using a carried total, deployed across all three replicas. I'm checking whether an earlier deploy could be responsible, but the metrics window covers healthy baseline performance stretching back before that earlier deploy, and the later rollback confirmation rules it out as the cause.

No other flag changes occurred in that hour, ruling those out too, and dependency checks aren't being pursued further. The real mechanism is that this rewrite made the computation scale quadratically with purchase count, since each render recomputes the full sum from scratch — and this got through because tests only covered small accounts, letting the quadratic blowup go unnoticed until larger purchase histories triggered it.

That quadratic code landed with deployment P2 of revision 5e07d73, replacing the prior approach of reading the account's carried total with this per-render loop; every replica ran it starting at T14, and rolling it back restored normal latency, which confirms the causal link. I'm also noting that requests take the default path unless one of the two rollout flags is set, so this issue affects everything outside those rollouts.

For contributing factors, I'm flagging that the tests covering this revision only checked correctness on accounts with a handful of purchases, never performance on large histories — had that been tested, the quadratic loop would've been caught pre-deploy. The proposed fix includes a test bounding reads, but I think a broader CI check for render performance on large histories is also worth proposing, and I'm noting the lack of canary/progressive rollout as a second contributing factor.

Since Argus handled the mitigation anyway, I'll classify the no-paging issue as a went_wrong item rather than a contributing factor, paired with an action item for improving detection/paging processes but leaving the specific answers open. On detection timing, I'll note the alert fired after the wait period without commenting on whether that speed was adequate. For action items, I'm proposing a CI check that bounds rendering cost for accounts with large purchase histories, covering all three spend figures rather than just the one already addressed.

I'm also adding a canary-style deployment gate for io-shop that holds promotion while p95 latency exceeds its pre-deploy baseline, and a process fix linking HighLatency alerts to an on-call rotation so someone actually gets paged.

For lessons learned: things that went well include Argus rolling back after the alert fired and confirming service recovery, the Investigator tying the slowdown to the deploy via the diff, and Code-Fix drafting PR #378 as a fix. What went wrong is that nobody was paged despite the alert — that's the main gap I'm capturing here.

For got_lucky, I'm noting that the latency never cascaded into failed requests or revenue loss, which could be luck, but the record doesn't confirm it was chance, so I'll leave that field empty rather than speculate.

The still_at_risk item is that the faulty revision remains at the head of the repo with automatic sync disabled, meaning the quadratic code is still what would deploy if sync were re-enabled — that's the lingering risk to flag.

In plain words: a code change made the account page recompute a shopper's average spend by re-summing their whole purchase history on every loop pass instead of reading a running total, so shoppers with long histories made pages much slower to build. The root cause is revision 5e07d73's rewrite of average_spend_per_item, called by every account-page render outside the two rollout flags, turning a simple sum into quadratic work per render. This reaches a real cause, and it isn't unrun — though I'm assuming the service-wide p95 is actually being driven by these account page renders.

For the symptom step I should say "the slowest requests" rather than giving a specific fraction. I'm checking which evidence to cite for step one — the onset and metric logs support it, but the ClientDisconnected log lines span a window before the onset too, with no clear rise, so I shouldn't cite those. I'm also looking at the earlier deploy P1 to confirm it shows latency at baseline, ruling it out as a cause.

action_items.item: Add a CI test that bounds the work of rendering the account page for an account with a large purchase history, on every spend-figure path, not only the lifetime average.
Add a canary stage to io-shop deployments that holds promotion while p95 latency is above its level before the deploy.
Link the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: From {began}, shoppers' requests to io-shop slowed down: the slowest requests took {series_while_broken} ms on average while it was broken and {series_at_worst} ms at worst, against {series_before} ms before it began. Failed requests did not rise beyond their normal variation.

Every account-page render outside both rollout flags computes the lifetime average spend per item. At the running revision, that computation re-sums the purchase list from its start once for every purchase in it, so its work grows quadratically with the account's purchase count. Only the last pass is kept.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 70dbcfde2b549d110a3817d92d60b6dd9786e78b. The metrics read show latency at its baseline with P1 in place up to the onset, and the confirmed rollback, which left the service on P1's revision, brought it back to normal.
A feature-flag change. The flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before.

causal_chain.step: That code arrived with deployment P2 of revision 5e07d73148d0a704b8fefe5f379bc652bb773655 at {P2.1}. The deploy replaced the read of the account's carried total with this loop. As of {T14.1}, all replicas ran that revision. Rolling it back brought the service off the incident's level, which confirmed it as the trigger.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change made the shop work out a shopper's average spend by adding up their purchase history again and again, once for each purchase, so account pages for shoppers with long histories took far longer to build.

contributing_factors.factor: The tests that came with the revision check only the average's value, and only for accounts with a handful of purchases. No test or check of how much work a render does for a long purchase history was seen before the deploy.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check on render cost for a large purchase history would have failed on the quadratic loop before the revision reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The revision reached every replica at once. No staged rollout and no latency gate on promotion was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A canary held back on rising latency would have exposed only part of the traffic, and the rollout would have stopped before every shopper was affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator read the deployment's diff and named the deploy as the candidate cause {T15.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent rolled the deployment back {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed, {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that the rollback had brought the service off the incident's level.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request #378 {T25.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert, so no person was brought in.

input.root_cause: Revision 5e07d73 rewrote average_spend_per_item, which every account-page render outside both rollout flags calls. It used to read the total the account carries. Now it re-sums the purchase list from its start on every loop iteration, and each pass is overwritten by the next. A render now does work that grows quadratically with the account's number of purchases, when only a single sum is needed.
input.still_at_risk: The code with the repeated re-summing is still in the repository, so any deploy from it before a fix is merged would bring the slowdown back.
input.symptom: Shop pages loaded slowly for shoppers
